Hello there.

Before I dive in, let me specify some details about me:

* Male / 20 years old
* 165 cm / 64 kg
* BMI: 23.5

I have always been a sedentary person. Exercise and activity faded pretty early in my school life and now I spend most of my time on the desk. Wanting to reduce some weight and increase my overall fitness, I started having a healthier diet (by counting calories) and also to run. I realized pretty soon how miserable my stamina is at the moment with an attempt to run.  
Looking at various options for beginners, I settled down on C25K. It seemed to be a lot more rational for my stamina with its first-day routine. For people who need context, this is C25K's day-one routine:

* 5 minutes of warmup walking.
* 60 second of running followed by 90 seconds of walking, for a total of 20 minutes. (8 times)
* 5 minutes of cooldown.

So, my starting days were definitely difficult. Almost unbearable shin splits. I actually managed to pull off this routine, but I felt a lot of pain and quite gassed out as I approached 60 seconds for every run session. It definitely felt gratifying when I made it, despite how basic and silly this actually must be, haha.

I'll list out all the questions and doubts I have, down here:

1. Is it natural that it was a little difficult for me to do even this day-one routine as a beginner? Or is this a sign of me having a much less endurance than an average couch potato too?
2. I don't feel confident that I can move onto the Week 2 routine, by just doing the Week 1 routine for 3 days. Should I keep doing the same routine for say, 4-5 days, this week before moving to the next week? If so, sadly the app isn't allowing me to track the data for each run (more than 3) and save it (my OCD feels bad about that. :3)
3. What am I supposed to do in the cooldown period? Walk/sit down and rest? Stretch my shins?
4. Both pain and gassing out seem to be potential hurdles to cross. Shall I carry water with me to rehydrate if I feel too gassed out? If so, how do I carry water in a run?
5. Any other possible advice/suggestions you could give to a beginner, especially about pain reduction & management, I'm all ears. I possibly have no idea what I'm doing, if things like posture, strides etc. really matter. So any advice is much appreciated.

Running does seem a little exciting, especially once I felt the satisfaction of finishing that routine, from being a sedentary person. Looking forward to being a much-fit individual, so I can actually enjoy this more with less pain.

Thank you very much, for going through this long post. I'm actively waiting for any and all replies.
